key_insight: Near no-slip stagnation points on solid surfaces, solute mixing switches from stretch-dominated algebraic decay to boundary-controlled exponential decay at a universal Péclet-dependent crossover time $t_B\sim Pe^{1/3}$.
engineering_relevance: This provides a predictive scaling law for contaminant transport and mixing near obstacles in porous media and wall-bounded flows, useful for designing reactors, filters, and remediation processes.
method: Analyze thin solute strips/sheets near separatrices ending at solid-boundary stagnation points
Derive asymptotic coupling between advection and diffusion near upstream stagnation points
Validate the theory against numerical simulations and extract scaling laws for $c_{\rm max}(t)$ and $\sigma(t)$
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a complete analytical theory that is explicitly validated by numerical simulations, with observed asymptotic scalings for concentration and width across regimes.
watch_item: The result is specialized to thin blobs near generic obstacles and no-slip stagnation points, so it may not transfer directly to open-flow stagnation points or more complex geometries without modification.
paper_title: Scalar mixing by stagnation points on solid surfaces
